samples.summary: New `PUT .../merges` 400 rule (MaxMergeEntries = 10,000) is not documented in the API reference table that documents every other merge limit
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:688-694 has a `| Rule | Behavior |` table for merges covering key format, key bounds, rs/cs, and "Span area — rs * cs at most 100,000". The delta adds a second, independently reachable 400 (`'merges' holds N entries, above the 10000 limit`, worksheet-settings.ts:141-145) with no corresponding row. The sibling structural caps are documented both there (line 627, `MaxAxisEntries`) and in docs/design/rest-api.md:289-304, so the repo's convention is that a caller-visible cap is written down; a client with a large imported sheet now gets a 400 whose rule appears nowhere.

samples.summary: Design doc still describes the freeze snap as "repeated until stable" after this delta replaced it with a single sorted sweep
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:120-123 says `setFreezePane` "pushes the boundary to the far edge of any block it would cut in half (`snapFreezePastMerges`, repeated until stable)". The delta removed the fixed-point loop in packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:217-253 in favour of one start-ordered sweep per axis, explicitly because the loop was quadratic in the merge count. The canonical subsystem doc is now describing an algorithm — and a performance characteristic — that no longer exists; the reason for the new shape (bounded, caller-supplied merge maps written wholesale by the v1 API) lives only in a source comment. The neighbouring paragraph (sheet.md:130-144) already documents the shared engine/controller contract, so this folds into the existing doc rather than needing a new one.

samples.summary: Merge-count cap is enforced only on the API writer, so a document the editor can legally reach (>10,000 merges, e.g. an xlsx import) can no longer be round-tripped through GET → PUT merges
samples.evidence: worksheet-settings.ts:140-145 rejects any map with more than 10,000 entries, but nothing in the engine bounds how many merges a worksheet may hold: `Sheet.mergeSelection` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4865) adds one at a time with no count check, and grep for `MaxMerge`/merge-count limits in packages/sheets/src found none. The `merges` endpoint is a replace-the-whole-field API (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-view.ts:258-300, "omitted merges are removed"), so the normal client shape is read-modify-write: on such a sheet `GET .../merges` returns 12,000 entries and PUTting them back — even unchanged — is a 400 with no way to express the edit. The cap is real and motivated, but it is enforced at one writer only, which makes the API strictly less expressive than the state the engine can already store.
searchedFor: grep setMerges across packages/cli and packages/sheets/src/store

samples.summary: `MaxMergeEntries` re-declares the literal 10,000 instead of importing the already-exported `MaxAxisEntries` it says it is derived from
samples.evidence: The doc comment at worksheet-settings.ts:38-41 states "10,000 is `MaxAxisEntries` in `worksheet-structure.ts`, itself the engine's `MaxAxisCoverage`", and that constant is exported (`export const MaxAxisEntries = 10000` at packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-structure.ts:56) and imported elsewhere in the backend (worksheet-structure-axis.controller.spec.ts:15). Keeping a second literal in the same directory means the stated derivation is only a comment; if the axis budget is retuned the two silently diverge. (A deliberate independent limit would be a fair answer — but then the comment should not tie it to the other one.)
